hook_text: A man holds the tail of a stumbling eland, painted on a rock long ago. What does it mean?
clip_script: Game Pass Shelter, in the Drakensberg. On the sandstone wall: red, white and brown eland, painted by San artists. One stumbles, dying. A figure holds its tail, legs crossed, hair on end. San rock art is found all over southern Africa: paintings in shelters, engravings on rocks. Paint came from ochre, charcoal and clay. Much of it is linked to San beliefs and healers. And two figures from the Linton panel now stand on South Africa's coat of arms.
visual_style: Whiteboard sandstone wall with eland painting themselves in red and white, then the coat of arms drawing its two greeting figures.
mood: Quiet and awe-filled, like standing in a sacred place.
pacing: Very slow reveal of the eland, then steady facts, ending on the coat of arms.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look closely at the coat of arms on a South African document.
